page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the ARMv8 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V2 processor model running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage and does not include integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 116,240.18 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,801.0. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, registering a top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 7,912.85 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 190.24 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 85,520.0, database operations at 49,949.23 in PassMark, and static web serving throughput of 123.05 GB/sec.

Given its high core density and dedicated ARM architecture, the c4a-highcpu-64 offers high resource density for compute-heavy workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is highly suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPUs limits its applicability for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or hardware-accelerated machine learning training.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is an ARM-based, compute-optimized server instance designed for high-density multi-threaded workloads. Powered by 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz, it features 128.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving throughput, alongside strong multi-core CPU capabilities. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is highly efficient for compute-intensive tasks such as software development pipelines, web serving, and database management, though workloads requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration will require alternative configurations.
